html:
The Classic Maya collapse was the decline and abandonment of the great Maya cities of the southern lowlands, in today's Guatemala, Belize and southern Mexico, during the 800s and 900s.

At their height, cities such as Tikal, Calakmul and Copán held tens of thousands of people. From about 800 kings stopped raising dated monuments, one city after another. Building ceased, and the population fell sharply over a few generations. The last known dated monument in the southern lowlands is from 909.

Scholars point to several causes working together: long droughts shown in lake and cave records, endless wars between the city-states, too many people for the land, and a loss of faith in divine kings. The Maya did not disappear; cities in the north such as Chichén Itzá flourished, and millions of Maya live in Guatemala today.
sum: The Classic Maya collapse was the decline and abandonment of the great Maya cities of the southern lowlands, in today's Guatemala, Belize and southern Mexico, during the 800s and 900s.
